objectives: "Computers play an important role in our daily life and in industry. For examples, most of processes in industry are controlled by computers; theoretical computation and molecular simulation are important tools for engineers and scientists for doing research and product development. The main purpose of this course is to introduce C++ as a programming tool for future chemical and material engineers. The course will take a pragmatic approach that incorporates actual engineering and science problems for its applications and examples."
content:
"1. Basic Concepts before Programming
2. Getting Started in C++
3. Assignment, Input, and Output
4. Selection
5. Repetition
6. Functions
7. Arrays
8. Data Files and File Streams
9. Additional Features
10. Pointers
11. Object-Oriented Programming (Classes)"
